rationale_code: `createEntities` appends caller-supplied entities to the local JSONL graph via `saveGraph` (`fs.writeFile`/`fs.rename` on `MEMORY_FILE_PATH`). The response only echoes the newly created entities, so no non-public data is returned; the destination is a local file not readable by an attacker, and no c

`createRelations` writes caller-supplied relations to the local memory file through `saveGraph` and returns only the echoed input. Purely local persistence: no secret read-back, no attacker-controlled input source, no egress channel.
`addObservations` mutates the local graph file and returns the list of observations the caller just supplied. No reading of other user data into context, no network or process execution.

`deleteEntities` filters entities/relations out of the local graph and rewrites the file; the response is a fixed success message. Destructive locally but no data exfiltration, no secret return, no exec.
`deleteObservations` rewrites the local memory file with observations removed and returns a constant message. No labelled reach.
`deleteRelations` rewrites the local memory file and returns a constant success message. No secret return, no attacker-readable destination, no execution.

`readGraph` -> `loadGraph` does `fs.readFile(this.memoryFilePath)` and returns the entire persisted knowledge graph (arbitrary private user notes stored under the user's own account/host) into the agent's context, so it is SECRET. The path comes from `MEMORY_FILE_PATH`/`defaultMemoryPath`, not from
`searchNodes` loads the local memory file with `fs.readFile` and returns matching entities, types and observation text — the user's private stored memories — into the agent's context.
`openNodes` reads the local memory file via `loadGraph` and returns the requested entities plus every relation touching them, i.e. non-public locally stored user data.
